local_help:
Resolve exact source names before requesting a route. English results are joined by stable IC ID to the Japanese name endpoint. Code lookup is Japanese only and may omit road information. Partial name enrichment appears in meta.warnings; missing values are null.

Usage:
  driveplaza-pp-cli interchanges [flags]

Examples:
  driveplaza-pp-cli interchanges --query nerima --language en --agent
  driveplaza-pp-cli interchanges --query 練馬 --language ja --agent
  driveplaza-pp-cli interchanges --code 1800001 --agent

Flags:
      --code string       Exact 7-digit interchange ID; Japanese code lookup, exclusive with --query
  -h, --help              help for interchanges
      --kind string       Interchange use: start or arrive; source suggestions can differ (default "start")
      --language string   Lookup language: ja or en; English rows also request Japanese names (default "ja")
      --limit int         Maximum results to return (1..30); output pagination only (default 10)
      --offset int        Skip this many matching records from the current source response
      --query string      Source name query; use canonical English spelling for --language en
      --road string       Restrict name results to this 4-digit source road ID

List source road IDs and bilingual road names

Usage:
  driveplaza-pp-cli roads [flags]

Examples:
  driveplaza-pp-cli roads --query tohoku --agent

Flags:
  -h, --help           help for roads
      --limit int      Maximum results to return (1..30); output pagination only (default 10)
      --offset int     Skip this many matching records from the current source response
      --query string   Case-insensitive local match against road ID, English or Japanese name

Explain source vehicle, time, priority and toll assumptions

Usage:
  driveplaza-pp-cli conditions [flags]

Examples:
  driveplaza-pp-cli conditions --agent

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for conditions

Request source estimates using exact English IC names and an explicit JST departure or arrival time. Minutes must be 00,10,20,30,40,50. --payment selects the source standard/ETC/ETC2.0 column and does not recompute discounts. ETC prices depend on actual eligibility and travel. Considering-traffic times are source estimates for the requested schedule. Use --detail for directional stop and forecast links.

Usage:
  driveplaza-pp-cli route [flags]

Examples:
  driveplaza-pp-cli route --from nerima --to sendai-minami --at 2026-10-10T08:00 --vehicle standard --payment etc --agent
  driveplaza-pp-cli route --from nerima --to sendai-minami --at 2026-10-10T08:00 --detail --agent

Flags:
      --at string          Planned JST time YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM; ten-minute increments only
      --detail             Include directional rest-stop identities and predicted-traffic handoff URLs
      --exclude-ordinary   Set the source form option to exclude ordinary roads
      --exclude-urban      Set the source form option to exclude urban expressways
      --from string        Exact English departure IC name from interchanges --language en
  -h, --help               help for route
      --payment string     Selected source toll column: standard, etc or etc2 (default "standard")
      --priority string    Source alternative ordering: time, distance or toll (default "time")
      --time-kind string   Meaning of --at: departure or arrival in JST (default "departure")
      --to string          Exact English arrival IC name from interchanges --kind arrive --language en
      --vehicle string     Source class: light, standard, medium, large or extra-large (default "standard")
      --via strings        Up to five exact English waypoint IC names, in route order

Use list for road-specific summaries, detail for facility sections and weekday hours, and facilities for source filter IDs. Up/down are provider direction identities. Availability and weekday hours do not establish that a facility is open now.

Usage:
  driveplaza-pp-cli sapa [flags]
  driveplaza-pp-cli sapa [command]

Available Commands:
  detail      Read a directional stop's source facilities and weekday hours
  facilities  List the source facility-selection IDs and labels
  list        List directional stops on a source road with facility evidence

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for sapa

Fetch one road response in English and Japanese, then paginate matching summaries locally. --query is local and case-insensitive, so it avoids the English form's case-sensitive name search. Facility filter semantics are the provider's selection; gray or none icons mean unavailable, missing icons mean unknown. The source's non-East data warning and weekday/holiday caveat stay attached.

Usage:
  driveplaza-pp-cli sapa list [flags]

Examples:
  driveplaza-pp-cli sapa list --road 1040 --direction up --limit 5 --agent
  driveplaza-pp-cli sapa list --road 1040 --query HASUDA --facility 9010 --agent

Flags:
      --direction string       Provider direction: up, down or both; identities remain distinct (default "both")
      --facility strings       Source facility IDs from sapa facilities, e.g.9010,5220
  -h, --help                   help for list
      --limit int              Maximum results to return (1..30); output pagination only (default 10)
      --max-scan-records int   Maximum source records to examine for local matching (1..2000), separate from --limit (default 500)
      --offset int             Skip this many matching records from the current source response
      --open-24                Request source selection for a 24-hour facility or service; not every shop
      --query string           Case-insensitive local match against English or Japanese stop name
      --road string            Required 4-digit road ID from roads; requests stay road-specific

      --offset int     Skip this many matching records from the current source response
      --query string   Case-insensitive local match against the exact advisory title
      --since string   Include source publication dates on/after YYYY-MM-DD in JST

Check CLI health

Usage:
  driveplaza-pp-cli doctor [flags]

Examples:
  driveplaza-pp-cli doctor
  driveplaza-pp-cli doctor --json
  driveplaza-pp-cli doctor --fail-on warn
  driveplaza-pp-cli doctor --fail-on stale

Flags:
      --fail-on string   Exit non-zero for selected health gates. stale: cache freshness plus errors; warn: path warnings plus errors; error: errors only. Default is never.
  -h, --help             help for doctor

which resolves a natural-language capability query (for example, "search messages" or "stale tickets") to the best matching command from this CLI's curated feature index.

Exit codes:
  0  at least one match found
  2  no confident match - the query did not score against any indexed capability; fall back to '--help' or 'search' if this CLI has one. Machine output (--json/--csv/--plain/--quiet, or a pipe) still exits 2 and writes {"matches":[]} (or the equivalent empty table) to stdout.

Usage:
  driveplaza-pp-cli which [query] [flags]

Examples:
  driveplaza-pp-cli which "stale tickets"
  driveplaza-pp-cli which "bottleneck"
  driveplaza-pp-cli which --limit 1 "send message"
  driveplaza-pp-cli which                                # list the full capability index

Flags:
  -h, --help        help for which
      --limit int   Maximum number of matches to return (default 3)

Returns prior learnings matching the supplied query by token-set
overlap (Jaccard >= 0.6) plus entity-aware validation. The LLM should
call this FIRST when starting work on a new user question; if
found=true AND results[0].entity_match == "exact" AND confidence >= 2,
the LLM can skip discovery and go straight to live fetch for the
returned resource IDs.

Empty match returns {"found": false, "results": []} with exit 0 — this
is an information query, not a not-found error.

Disabling: DRIVEPLAZA_NO_LEARN=true returns the empty shape even
when learnings exist.

Usage:
  driveplaza-pp-cli recall <query> [flags]

Examples:
  QUERY="$(cat /path/to/question.txt)" driveplaza-pp-cli recall "$QUERY" --agent
  QUERY="$(cat /path/to/question.txt)" driveplaza-pp-cli recall "$QUERY" --agent --min-confidence 2

Flags:
      --db string            SQLite database file path (default: resolved data directory data.db)
      --debug-mismatches     Include cross-entity mismatches in the envelope under mismatches[]
  -h, --help                 help for recall
      --limit int            Maximum number of learnings to return (default 10)
      --min-confidence int   Minimum confidence to include in results (default 1)

Record one or more "this query -> this resource" mappings so the next
query that matches surfaces the right resources without re-running discovery.

This command is designed to be backgrounded by an LLM right before it
emits the user-facing response: silent on success, errors only to
the CLI state directory's teach.log, safe to fire-and-forget.

Disabling: pass --no-learn or set DRIVEPLAZA_NO_LEARN=true.

Usage:
  driveplaza-pp-cli teach [flags]

Examples:
  driveplaza-pp-cli teach --query "find items in category" --resource-type items --resource GROUP-category

Flags:
      --db string                    SQLite database file path (default: resolved data directory data.db)
  -h, --help                         help for teach
      --no-validate                  Suppress teach-time resource-shape validation (warnings to teach.log)
      --notes string                 Optional free-form note recorded in the audit log
      --playbook-file string         Optional path to a JSON playbook recording the CLI choreography for this query family
      --playbook-json string         Optional inline JSON playbook (mutually exclusive with --playbook-file; for agents without filesystem access)
      --playbook-notes string        Optional inline gotchas/workarounds for this query family (stored alongside the playbook)
      --playbook-notes-file string   Optional path to a markdown file with playbook notes
      --query string                 User's original natural-language question (required)
      --quiet                        Silent on success (default true — designed for background invocation) (default true)
      --resource strings             Resource ID — repeat for multiple (required)
      --resource-type string         Resource type (required; e.g. matches a row in the local resources table)
      --venue string                 Optional venue scope tag stored with the learning

Surface for browsing, filtering, and deleting rows in the
search_learnings table that the LLM populates via the 'teach' command.

Usage:
  driveplaza-pp-cli learnings [flags]
  driveplaza-pp-cli learnings [command]

Available Commands:
  candidates  List auto-captured improvement candidates awaiting judgment
  confirm     Confirm an open candidate: print its full payload, then materialize it
  forget      Delete learnings matching a query (use --all to wipe every rule for that query)
  list        List recorded learnings
  purge       Delete settled candidate rows (expired and confirmed; --tombstones adds rejected)
  reject      Reject a candidate and tombstone its derivation signature
  stats       Report learn-loop effectiveness metrics from the local events table

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for learnings

Profiles capture a set of flag values under a name so a scheduled
agent can invoke the same command with the same configuration each run.

  profile save <name>         captures the current invocation's set flags
  profile use <name>          prints the values (for inspection)
  profile list                lists all saved profiles
  profile show <name>         shows the values of one profile
  profile delete <name>       removes a profile

Use --profile <name> on any command to apply that profile's values.
Explicit flags override profile values.

Usage:
  driveplaza-pp-cli profile [flags]
  driveplaza-pp-cli profile [command]

Available Commands:
  delete      Remove a profile
  list        List saved profiles
  save        Save the current invocation's non-default flags as a named profile
  show        Show a profile's values as JSON
  use         Print the flag values a profile will apply (does not execute anything)

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for profile

Browse API resource interfaces using their raw command names.

Promoted top-level commands cover single-endpoint shortcuts. This
command lists resource parents that group multiple endpoints.

Run 'api' with no arguments to list those interfaces.
Run 'api <interface>' to see that interface's methods.

Usage:
  driveplaza-pp-cli api [interface] [flags]

Examples:
  # List all available interfaces
  driveplaza-pp-cli api

  # Show methods for a specific interface
  driveplaza-pp-cli api <interface-name>

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for api

agents can introspect this CLI at runtime without parsing --help or

Usage:
  driveplaza-pp-cli agent-context [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help     help for agent-context
      --pretty   indent JSON output for human reading

Inspect or amend stored CLI playbooks

Usage:
  driveplaza-pp-cli playbook [flags]
  driveplaza-pp-cli playbook [command]

Available Commands:
  amend       Append a note to an existing playbook (LLM-fired self-correction, silent)
  list        List stored playbooks (query_family, content presence, last observed)

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for playbook

Adds one row to entity_lookups. Used by the recall path's pattern
engine to substitute values for canonical names at substitution time.
Computed kinds (lowercase, uppercase, kebab-case, capitalize-first, slug)
cannot be taught — they are derived from the canonical input.

Usage:
  driveplaza-pp-cli teach-lookup [flags]

Examples:
  driveplaza-pp-cli teach-lookup --kind country --canonical "United States" --value USA

Flags:
      --canonical string   Canonical entity name (required)
      --db string          SQLite database file path (default: resolved data directory data.db)
  -h, --help               help for teach-lookup
      --kind string        Entity kind, e.g. country, team (required, must not be a computed kind)
      --value string       Value/alias that should resolve to the canonical (required)

Adds one row to search_patterns. The recall path uses patterns to
substitute live query entities into a resource template, so a pattern
with query_template="items in {entity}" and
resource_template="GROUP-{entity:category}" generalizes one teach into
a whole family.

Usage:
  driveplaza-pp-cli teach-pattern [flags]

Examples:
  driveplaza-pp-cli teach-pattern --query-template "items in {entity}" --resource-template "GROUP-{entity:category}" --resource-type items --entity-kind category --strategy substitute

Flags:
      --db string                  SQLite database file path (default: resolved data directory data.db)
      --entity-kind string         Entity kind name registered in entity_lookups (required)
  -h, --help                       help for teach-pattern
      --query-template string      Query template with {entity} placeholder (required)
      --resource-template string   Resource template with typed entity slot, e.g. PREFIX-{entity:country} (required)
      --resource-type string       Resource type for substituted IDs (required)
      --strategy string            Substitution strategy: substitute | substitute-then-search-prefix (default substitute)
      --venue string               Optional venue scope tag

Stores a structured CLI command sequence (with entity slots) and/or
free-form gotchas/workarounds, keyed on the structural query family.
The recall path surfaces this whenever a future query of the same
family fires, so the agent can replay the choreography and read the
notes verbatim.

At least one of --playbook-json/--playbook-file and --notes/--notes-file
must be set. --playbook-json takes the playbook body inline so MCP-only
agents can record playbooks without a file on disk.

Usage:
  driveplaza-pp-cli teach-playbook [flags]

Examples:
  driveplaza-pp-cli teach-playbook --query "find items in category" --notes "example playbook note"

Flags:
      --db string              Database path (default: standard cache location)
  -h, --help                   help for teach-playbook
      --notes string           Free-text notes (gotchas, workarounds) -- mutually exclusive with --notes-file
      --notes-file string      Path to a markdown file with the notes
      --playbook-file string   Path to a JSON file with the playbook (steps, entity_slots, expected_tool_calls)
      --playbook-json string   Inline playbook JSON (steps, entity_slots, expected_tool_calls) -- mutually exclusive with --playbook-file
      --query string           Example query that anchors the family (required)

Feedback is captured locally first in the CLI data directory's feedback.jsonl.
When `DRIVEPLAZA_FEEDBACK_ENDPOINT` is set and either --send is
passed or `DRIVEPLAZA_FEEDBACK_AUTO_SEND=true`, the entry is
POSTed as JSON after the local write.

Write what surprised you or tripped you up, not a bug report. The
loop is: agent notices friction -> one invocation -> captured -> the
maintainer sees it.

Usage:
  driveplaza-pp-cli feedback [text] [flags]
  driveplaza-pp-cli feedback [command]

Examples:
  driveplaza-pp-cli feedback "docs said exclusive but the boundary is inclusive"
  driveplaza-pp-cli feedback --stdin < notes.txt
  driveplaza-pp-cli feedback list

Available Commands:
  list        List recent feedback entries

Flags:
  -h, --help    help for feedback
      --send    POST to the configured feedback endpoint in addition to local write
      --stdin   Read feedback body from stdin rather than arguments
